architecture.mechanism: Superhydrophobic surfaces cause impinging water droplets to bead, roll off, and shed before freezing, so ice accretion and adhesion on the blade surface are reduced.
architecture.intervention: Coat the leading edges and outer blade spans with a salt-tolerant superhydrophobic coating whose micro/nano texture is engineered to retain repellency under salt spray and high-wind erosion, validated under Bohai-Sea-simulated winter icing conditions.
architecture.expected_effect: Less atmospheric ice accumulates on the blades and any adhered ice bonds more weakly, preserving the aerodynamic profile and restoring winter power output while surviving the offshore salt/wind environment.
architecture.falsification_test: Expose coated and uncoated blade coupons to an icing wind tunnel at high-velocity airflow with cyclic salt spray and supercooled droplet injection; measure ice accretion mass, adhesion strength, and contact angle after repeated salt-aging cycles — if the coated coupons show no statistically significant reduction in ice mass and adhesion after salt exposure, the mechanism is falsified.
